dump.name: gtfo-inspection/dumper/dump.cs
dump.note: Local read-only copy used for this audit. dump.cs records the short type name, the il2cpp RVA and the exact parameter list.

question: Which number is the site's `gear-block` reference, and can a gtfo.equipment instance read that same number back from the game?

answer.reference: GameData.PlayerOfflineGearDataBlock.persistentID, written as plain decimal text in the catalog (the site spells it with String(blockId): digits only, no sign, no leading zero)
answer.match: Ordinal text comparison of the reference against the record's text after the `OfflineGear_ID_` prefix. Nothing is parsed or normalized: a second spelling of one block id (leading zeros, a sign, surrounding space, a decimal point, a radix prefix) is a different string and matches nothing, so no numeric equality path exists.

method: Read-only static analysis. No assembly is loaded into the CLR, no game process is started, nothing is written to a profile or to the game directory.
Interop metadata was read with ilspycmd (members and signatures only): Gear.GearIDRange, Player.BackpackItem, Player.PlayerBackpack, Gear.GearManager, GameData.PlayerOfflineGearDataBlock.

Native bodies were decoded with Iced x64 at the RVAs dump.cs records. Game code lives in the PE section named `il2cpp`; callers are literal E8 rel32 sites, and indirect dispatch (vtable call, delegate Invoke, register) is not resolved, so a method with no listed caller may still run through one of those.

String literals were read from global-metadata.dat (header 0xFAB11BAF, version 24) through its stringLiteral table; a litOffset is an index into that table, and the same value is also encoded in the `ldc.i4` before each metadata literal load in the decoded body.

fields.note: The generic GameDataBlockBase`1 layout is not spelled out in dump.cs; the subclass offsets below pin it.

chain.meaning: Iterates the GameData.PlayerOfflineGearDataBlock list, skips a block whose Type is not 1 or 2 or whose GearJSON is empty, then builds the instance id as String.Concat(<literal>, boxed block.persistentID) and calls ParseAndStashGear(block.name, instanceId, block.GearJSON, null, ref this.m_gearPerSlot, block.Type). Sites: 0x13302E8 (Type at +0x40), 0x1330300 (GearJSON at +0x48), 0x1330355 (persistentID at +0x38), 0x13303B6 (call).
chain.reason: This is the game's own loader; nothing in the plugin calls it or writes a datablock. It is recorded because it is the only place that spells the gear block id onto a gear.

chain.meaning: The literal LoadOfflineGearDatas concatenates the block id onto; the other literal it loads in the same body is the empty string used for the GearJSON test. Confirmed out of game by the game's own favorites record: GTFO_Favorites.txt holds "LastEquipped_Standard": "OfflineGear_ID_34" and the Modded profile's GTFO_Favorites.json holds "OfflineGear_ID_14"/"OfflineGear_ID_57", which is the string GearManager.CheckLastEquipped compares against a gear's PlayfabItemInstanceId.

Creates `new GearIDRange(gearJSON)` (0x1330D01) and writes the two strings and the offline type onto it: [gear+0x20] = itemId (0x1330D19), [gear+0x28] = instanceId (0x1330D28), [gear+0x30] = offlineType (0x1330D3C). The offsets are the three backing fields dump.cs declares for GearIDRange.
chain.reason: The record it writes is what the matcher reads; the method itself is not called by the plugin.

chain.meaning: Picks the slot's gear out of m_lastEquippedGearPerSlot (+0x40), m_favoriteGearPerSlot (+0x38) and m_gearPerSlot (+0x30) and calls EquipLocalGear at 0x133093C with that stored GearIDRange object; an element read out of m_gearPerSlot reaches its GearIDRange through the element's +0x20 field.

directCallers.signature: System.Void Gear.GearManager::SetupGearInOfflineMode() (tail jmp, not an E8 edge)

chain.reason: Recorded to show that the object built by ParseAndStashGear is the object that is equipped, not a rebuilt copy.

chain.meaning: Both hand the GearIDRange object on to Player.PlayerBackpack::SpawnAndEquipGearAsync (0x1761100), which stores it through Player.PlayerBackpack::CreateAndStoreBackpackItem(Item,Player.InventorySlot,Gear.GearIDRange) (0x175EE40) into Player.BackpackItem.GearIDRange.
chain.reason: The path that carries the offline record into the backpack item the matcher reads back.

refusals.meaning: The synced packet carries only Comps/Mod/MatTrans/publicName, so a gear rebuilt from a packet reads no offline block id. The matcher answers false for it, which is the same answer a gear that never came from an offline block gets.

Component 2 (Category) holds the GearCategoryDataBlock.persistentID. The site exports that block with the same number as state.blockId, but it is a different block's id, so it is not used as the mount key.
The existing resource key. It identifies a gear definition but is not the block id, so it is never compared against a gear-block reference.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed, and a direct call edge only proves that a call site exists in the shipped binary.

The prefix is identified from the metadata literal table plus the game's own favorites file; a build that renamed it would make a gear-block mount match nothing rather than match wrongly, which is why the read is spelled as an exact prefix plus the rest of the record and the comparison is ordinal. A record whose suffix is not plain decimal text (for example a zero-padded id) reads no block id at all instead of being parsed.

Whether the game keeps the BackpackItem.GearIDRange object alive for every equip path is not verified in game; the matcher re-reads the current backpack item on every dispatch and answers false when the record is absent.
